At {PLACE} he holds {ITEM} up against the trees: close, but not quite.
At {PLACE} the light is right, but the angle is wrong.
At {PLACE} the roofs line up with {ITEM} at last.
From {PLACE} it is the very view, only the trees are taller.
Back at {PLACE}, {GIVER} sets up an easel to paint it again.
At {PLACE} {GIVER} writes the place's name on the back of {ITEM}.

twists: An old man at the spot says his grandfather sat for that painter.
A new building now hides half of the view.
good: {GIVER} paints the view again, with him in the corner.
The gallery hangs {ITEM} with a label: found by a walker.
worse: It was a view that doesn't exist: the painter made it up.
He finds the spot, but it is a car park now.

quests.title: The Palm Reader's Hunch
items: a deck of worn tarot cards
a palm drawn on a napkin

say: At {PLACE} {GIVER} takes his hand and frowns: there is a love in it he hasn't met yet.
{GIVER} at {PLACE} swings {ITEM} over his palm: a place he will love, it says, and one he will hate.
At {PLACE} he waits to feel something. He feels something.
At {PLACE} {ITEM} spins on its own, just for a moment.
At {PLACE} he sits a while and thinks about what he really likes.
At {PLACE} a crow lands next to him and looks him in the eye.
Back at {PLACE}, {GIVER} nods: he knows himself a bit better now.
At {PLACE} {GIVER} says the lines on his hand have moved.

twists: {GIVER} reads his other hand and says the opposite.
The cards come up the same three times in a row.
good: Whatever it was, he walks off lighter.
{GIVER} won't take any money: 'You'll know when you get there.'
worse: {GIVER} admits it was the same reading for everyone today.
It rains on the way, and the hunch washes off.

quests.title: The Traveller's Photos
items: a camera full of travel photos
a roll of film from far away

say: At {PLACE}, {GIVER} has lost {ITEM}, with a year of travels on it.
{GIVER} at {PLACE} is close to tears: {ITEM} is gone, and every far-off sight with it.
He asks around at {PLACE}, and someone saw {ITEM} left on a bench.
At {PLACE} a cleaner hands over {ITEM} from the lost and found.
Back at {PLACE}, {GIVER} shows him every photo, one sight after another.
At {PLACE}, {GIVER} tells him about each place over a long coffee.

twists: One photo is of a place on his own bucket list.
The journal ends with a list of dreams, half of them ticked off.
good: {GIVER} hugs him and says: go and see them yourself. He looks at his bucket list with new eyes.
They swap bucket lists, and he promises to send a postcard from the first sight he ticks off.
worse: The photos are all of the same cat; still, {GIVER} is grateful.
Half the film is ruined, but the stories are not.

events.title: A lamp in the window
text: A lamp is lit in the window of {PLACE}, long after closing.
The door of {PLACE} stands ajar after midnight, and something inside glitters.

win.say: The owner lets him try a ring that tingles; a little Magic stays on his finger.

lose.say: By the time he gets there the lamp is out and the door locked.

events.missed: Someone saw a lamp in the window of {PLACE} after midnight.

events.title: A shimmer in the stones
text: The air between the old stones of {PLACE} shimmers like a heat haze, at night.
Through the arch at {PLACE} he glimpses a street that isn't here.

win.say: He reaches in, and his hand comes back cold, smelling of another city's rain; a little Magic clings to it.

lose.say: A tram rattles by and the shimmer is gone.

events.missed: People say the stones of {PLACE} shimmered last night.

events.title: A shadow under the water
text: Something long and dark moves under the water off {PLACE}, bigger than any boat.
The boats at {PLACE} rock all at once on a calm day, and the gulls go quiet.

win.say: He waits at the edge and a huge eye looks back at him, then blinks, friendly.

lose.say: He looks away for a second and the shadow is gone.

events.missed: People at {PLACE} swear something huge swam past today.

events.title: The night bus singer
text: A man at {PLACE} is singing to the empty stop, and he isn't bad at all.
Someone at {PLACE} starts a song while everyone waits for the last bus.

win.say: He joins in on the chorus, and the whole stop claps when the bus pulls up.

lose.say: He gets the words wrong, and the singer gives him a long look.

events.missed: People at {PLACE} say someone sang the whole stop to sleep last night.

events.title: The baker's first batch
text: The light is on at {PLACE} long before opening; the baker is a pair of hands short.
Flour dust drifts out of the back door of {PLACE} in the dark.

win.say: He kneads till his arms ache and leaves with a warm loaf.

lose.say: He drops a whole tray, and the baker sends him home.

events.missed: {PLACE} opened late today; the baker was alone at the ovens.

events.title: A cat on the roof
text: A cat is crying on the roof above {PLACE}, and a small crowd is pointing.
Someone's cat has climbed onto the awning of {PLACE} and won't come down.

win.say: He climbs up, and the cat walks into his arms as if it planned it.

lose.say: The cat jumps down on its own the moment he's halfway up.

events.missed: The cat on {PLACE} came down by itself in the end.

events.title: A chess game in the street
text: Two old men play chess at {PLACE}, and one of them needs a partner.
A board is set up at {PLACE} with a sign: 'beat me, win a coffee'.

win.say: He wins in twenty moves, and gets his coffee.

lose.say: He's checkmated before he finds his feet.

events.missed: The chess player at {PLACE} beat everyone today.

events.title: A night market
text: Stalls are going up at {PLACE} after dark, with lanterns and the smell of grilled corn.
A night market fills {PLACE}; one stall-holder is shouting for help with a tent.

win.say: He helps put up the tent and is paid in grilled corn.

lose.say: The tent comes down on top of them both.

events.missed: {PLACE} had a night market; he only saw the lanterns being packed.

events.title: A circle of mushrooms
text: A perfect circle of mushrooms has come up overnight on the grass at {PLACE}.
The dew at {PLACE} lies in a ring this morning, and the grass inside is dry.

win.say: He walks round it three times the right way, and the morning feels lucky.

lose.say: A gardener mows it before he gets there.

events.missed: People say a fairy ring came up at {PLACE} this morning.

events.title: Humming stones
text: The old stones of {PLACE} are humming tonight.
A faint glow runs along the ground at {PLACE}, where the ley lines meet.

win.say: He stands still and listens until the hum fills him up.

lose.say: A bus goes past and the hum is gone.

events.missed: People say the stones at {PLACE} hummed all night.

events.title: Oven trouble
text: The oven at {PLACE} broke down before the morning rush.
Smoke and shouting at {PLACE}: the oven is dead.

win.say: He carries flour and fetches a part; bread is out on time.

lose.say: They can't fix it in time. No bread this morning.

events.missed: Word is the bakery at {PLACE} had no bread this morning.

events.title: Pastries for helpers
text: {PLACE} is giving free pastries to everyone who helped.

win.say: He gets the biggest one.

lose.say: Only crumbs left by the time he gets there.

events.missed: The free pastries at {PLACE} are all gone.

events.title: Bread shortage
text: A long queue for the last bread at {PLACE}.

win.say: He lets an old lady go first; she shares her loaf.

lose.say: Sold out right before him.

events.missed: The bread at {PLACE} sold out by ten.

events.title: Market setup
text: Stallholders by {PLACE} are short of hands to set up the market.
Tarps and poles everywhere at {PLACE}: the market needs help.

win.say: He raises three stalls; the traders give him a discount card.

lose.say: Half the stalls stay packed; the market is thin today.

events.missed: The market by {PLACE} opened late and half empty.

events.title: Market bargains
text: The market by {PLACE} is in full swing, with bargains for helpers.

win.say: He haggles a fine deal.

lose.say: He pays the tourist price.

events.missed: The market by {PLACE} packed up for the day.

events.title: School run
text: The crossing guard at {PLACE} is off sick and the kids are arriving.

win.say: He helps every child across; one gives him a drawing.

lose.say: A backpack got left on the pavement.

events.missed: Parents by {PLACE} are grumbling about the crossing.

events.title: The lost backpack
text: A child's backpack is waiting to be claimed at {PLACE}.

win.say: He finds the owner by the name on the lunchbox.

lose.say: Nobody claims it yet.

events.missed: The backpack at {PLACE} went home with a teacher.

events.title: Lost child
text: A parent at {PLACE} has lost sight of their child.
A call goes out across {PLACE}: a little boy is missing.

win.say: He finds the child by the ice cream stand; hugs all round.

lose.say: The search goes on without luck.

events.missed: The child lost at {PLACE} was found safe, they say.

events.title: The big search
text: Volunteers gather at {PLACE} to search for the missing child.

win.say: He spots the child asleep under a slide. Found!

lose.say: Someone else finds the child first. Phew, anyway.

events.missed: The search from {PLACE} ended well.

events.title: Escaped parrot
text: A parrot has escaped from {PLACE} and is swearing at pigeons.
A green parrot shouts 'hello!' from a tree near {PLACE}.

win.say: The parrot lands on his shoulder. It learns his name.

lose.say: It flies off over the roofs.

events.missed: People near {PLACE} still hear a parrot shouting 'hello'.

events.title: Parrot sighting
text: The runaway parrot was seen near {PLACE}.

win.say: He coaxes it down with a cracker.

lose.say: Gone again, laughing.

events.missed: The parrot near {PLACE} found its own way home.

events.title: Cafe rush hour
text: A bus of tourists has just walked into {PLACE}; the barista is alone.

win.say: He clears tables and takes orders; tips for everyone.

lose.say: Queues out the door; a grumpy reviewer is in it.

events.missed: {PLACE} got a one-star review for slow service.

events.title: The grumpy reviewer
text: A food critic is scowling at a table in {PLACE}.

win.say: He chats with the critic, who softens. Four stars!

lose.say: The critic writes 'tepid' in big letters.

events.missed: The review of {PLACE} is out. It is not kind.

events.title: Stranded passengers
text: All trains are delayed at {PLACE}; tired passengers fill the hall.
A signal failure strands hundreds at {PLACE}.

win.say: He hands out water and starts a sing-along.

lose.say: Tempers run short; he keeps out of it.

events.missed: The trains at {PLACE} ran an hour late.

events.title: Fun run marshal
text: A charity fun run starts at {PLACE} and needs marshals.

win.say: He cheers every runner past; they give him a medal too.

lose.say: A runner trips at his corner.

events.missed: The fun run at {PLACE} raised a lot of money.

events.title: First aid
text: A runner with a twisted ankle waits at {PLACE}.

win.say: He wraps it neatly; the runner limps home happy.

lose.say: He makes it worse, then better.

events.missed: The runner at {PLACE} got patched up.

events.title: Book sale
text: {PLACE} has crates of books to sort for a sale.

win.say: He finds a rare first edition while sorting.

lose.say: Most crates go to recycling.

events.missed: The book sale at {PLACE} is over.

events.title: Protest at the town hall
text: Neighbours protest at {PLACE} about a park being sold.
Placards and drums outside {PLACE}.

win.say: He helps both sides talk; a new bench is promised.

lose.say: Nobody listens to anyone. A strike is called.

events.missed: The protest at {PLACE} ended with nothing agreed.

events.title: Bus strike
text: The buses at {PLACE} are on strike; late workers have to walk.

win.say: He walks a nurse home; the drivers wave him through later.

lose.say: Everyone walks, grumbling.

events.missed: The strike at {PLACE} is over.

events.title: A song for a crowd
text: A street musician at {PLACE} is playing to no one.

win.say: He gathers a crowd; the musician writes him into a song.

lose.say: The musician packs up and leaves town.

events.missed: The music at {PLACE} has stopped.

events.title: Market in the rain
text: A sudden shower soaks the stalls by {PLACE}.

win.say: He holds the tarps; the farmers give him a bag of apples.

lose.say: Half the fruit is ruined.

events.missed: The stalls by {PLACE} were drowned out.

events.title: Match day
text: A fan near {PLACE} has lost his ticket to the big game.

win.say: He finds the ticket in a hedge; the fan takes him along.

lose.say: No ticket; the bars fill with gloomy fans.

events.missed: The home team lost; {PLACE} is quiet tonight.

events.title: The inspector is coming
text: The health inspector is due at {PLACE} in half an hour, and the kitchen is a mess.

win.say: He scrubs until it shines; top marks.

lose.say: A low score goes up in the window.

events.missed: {PLACE} has a new score on the door. Not a good one.

events.title: Flu season
text: The queue at {PLACE} runs round the block: flu is going about.

win.say: He delivers medicine to three old neighbours.

lose.say: He catches a sniffle himself.

events.missed: The flu queue at {PLACE} is finally shorter.

events.title: No photographer
text: A wedding at {PLACE}, and the photographer hasn't turned up.
A bride at {PLACE} is close to tears: no photographer.

win.say: He takes the photos; one is perfect. They give him cake.

lose.say: All his photos are a bit blurry.

events.missed: The wedding at {PLACE} went ahead with phone pictures.

events.title: Testing the ice
text: {PLACE} opens today and needs someone brave to test the ice.

win.say: He glides round once without falling. Free skating!

lose.say: He falls on his bottom, to applause.

events.missed: {PLACE} opened without him.

events.title: Lifeguard short
text: {PLACE} is packed and short of a lifeguard.

win.say: He blows the whistle all afternoon; a little paid shift.

lose.say: They close the deep end.

events.missed: {PLACE} closed early today.

events.title: Power cut
text: The lights go out at {PLACE} halfway through the show.

win.say: He tells stories by candlelight; free tickets for next time.

lose.say: Refund queue. Long refund queue.

events.missed: The show at {PLACE} was called off.

events.title: Lost phone
text: A phone keeps ringing under a seat at {PLACE}.

win.say: He finds the owner from her lock screen; VIP pass for him.

lose.say: He hands it in at the bar.

events.missed: The phone at {PLACE} went to lost property.

events.title: Stargazing night
text: The astronomy club is setting up telescopes at {PLACE}.

win.say: He spots Saturn's rings and they let him name a little star.

lose.say: Clouds roll in.

events.missed: The stargazers at {PLACE} went home.

events.title: Shop alarm
text: The alarm at {PLACE} is wailing; the shopkeeper thinks it's a robbery.

win.say: It was a cat. He calms everyone; free snack for life.

lose.say: Everybody shouts. The shop closes early.

events.missed: {PLACE} closed early after a scare.

events.title: Night porter
text: {PLACE} is short of porters tonight.

win.say: He carries linen and cheers up a ward. Paid shift.

lose.say: He gets lost in the corridors for an hour.

events.missed: The nurses at {PLACE} had a long night.

events.title: Fire drill
text: The alarm goes off at {PLACE}: a drill, but nobody knows that.

win.say: He guides everyone out calmly; a firefighter gives him a badge.

lose.say: Chaos on the stairs, but everyone gets out.

events.missed: The drill at {PLACE} took an hour.

events.title: Street party
text: A street party is starting near {PLACE}; they need someone for the music.
Bunting goes up around {PLACE}: party tonight!

win.say: He runs the music and the whole street dances.

lose.say: The speaker dies; everyone sings instead.

events.missed: The street party near {PLACE} went on until late.

events.title: Tour group lost
text: A tour group at {PLACE} lost their guide.

win.say: He leads them round and they tip him.

lose.say: He gets them lost too, briefly.

events.missed: The tour group at {PLACE} found their guide.

events.title: The big delivery
text: A lorry is stuck outside {PLACE} and the driver needs help unloading.

win.say: He unloads it all; the driver pays him and gives him a lift tip.

lose.say: A box breaks open: oranges everywhere.

events.missed: The lorry outside {PLACE} finally left.

events.title: The museum moves
text: {PLACE} is moving to a new building and needs every pair of hands.

win.say: Box after box; they put his name on a little plaque.

lose.say: The move stalls; boxes everywhere.

events.missed: {PLACE} moved without him.

events.title: Stray boxes
text: Boxes from the stalled move are piling up at {PLACE}.

win.say: He sorts them and finds a lost painting.

lose.say: He sorts them into the wrong piles.

events.missed: The boxes at {PLACE} were cleared away.

events.title: Clean-up day
text: It's clean-up day; volunteers meet at {PLACE} with bin bags.

win.say: The park sparkles; flower beds get planted.

lose.say: Not enough hands; the pigeons win today.

events.missed: Clean-up day at {PLACE} is over.

events.title: Sparks at the tower
text: Purple sparks fly from {PLACE}; a spell has got loose.

win.say: He shuts the right window and the spell fizzles. The wizard nods.

lose.say: Everything nearby smells of lavender for a day.

events.missed: The sparks at {PLACE} died down.

events.title: Star party
text: Someone has set up telescopes at {PLACE} and invites anyone to look.

win.say: He waits his turn and sees the rings of Saturn. He can't stop talking about it.

lose.say: By his turn the clouds roll in; he sees a lens cap.

events.missed: The star party at {PLACE} packed up at dawn.

events.title: Lights at the castle
text: Odd lights flicker at {PLACE} tonight.

win.say: He follows them and finds an old coin in the grass.

lose.say: Just teenagers with torches.

events.missed: The lights at {PLACE} were gone by morning.

events.title: Guild muster
text: The bell rings at {PLACE}: the guild needs volunteers today.

win.say: He hauls, lifts and fetches; the guild cheers him.

lose.say: He arrives as they finish, but they give him a cup of tea.

events.missed: The guild at {PLACE} managed without him.

events.title: Story circle
text: A fire is lit by {PLACE} and people gather for tales.

win.say: He tells the tale of his travels, and they hang on every word.

lose.say: He forgets the end, but the fire is warm.

events.missed: The story circle by {PLACE} has gone home.

events.title: Stop, thief!
text: Someone shouts 'Stop, thief!' at {PLACE} and a bag snatcher runs past.
A tourist at {PLACE} screams: her phone is gone, and a man is sprinting off.

win.say: He trips the thief up and holds him until the police come. People clap.

lose.say: He gives chase, but the thief is faster. He walks the tourist to the police.

events.missed: Someone snatched a bag at {PLACE}; the thief got away.

events.title: A shell game
text: A man at {PLACE} moves three cups very fast: find the pea, double your money.
At {PLACE} a crowd watches a shell game, and a 'lucky winner' cheers a bit too loud.

win.say: He spots the trick, plays the man at his own game and walks off with the pot.

lose.say: There was never a pea. He walks off before betting, a little wiser.

events.missed: The shell game at {PLACE} has moved on, with everybody's money.

events.title: A charity run
text: A charity run starts at {PLACE}, and they're short of runners.
At {PLACE} people in matching T-shirts warm up for a charity run.

win.say: He runs the whole way and raises more than anyone. Photo on the finish line.

lose.say: He walks the last bit, but every step counted for the charity.

events.missed: The charity run at {PLACE} has finished; the stalls are packing up.

events.title: A police checkpoint
text: The police have set up a checkpoint at {PLACE} and are asking questions.
At {PLACE} two officers are checking papers.

win.say: He chats with the officers, helps a lost tourist with directions, and they wave him through with a smile.

lose.say: They search his bag for twenty minutes, then let him go.

events.missed: The checkpoint at {PLACE} has packed up.

events.title: A pigeon that talks
text: A grey pigeon at {PLACE} is asking passers-by, very politely, for directions.
At {PLACE} a pigeon clears its throat and asks the time.

win.say: He walks the pigeon to its old roost; it drops him a shiny coin from 1920.

lose.say: He tries, but the pigeon is offended by his accent and flies off.

events.missed: People at {PLACE} talk about a pigeon that asked for the time.

events.title: The stopped clock
text: The big clock at {PLACE} has stopped, and everyone under it stands very still.
At {PLACE} the clock hands stand still, and so do the pigeons in the air.

win.say: He nudges the minute hand back to work; the square breathes out and nobody remembers a thing.

lose.say: He can't reach the hand. The clock starts again by itself, a minute late for ever.

events.missed: The clock at {PLACE} lost a minute today, and nobody can say how.

events.title: The lantern walk
text: Paper lanterns drift along {PLACE} with nobody carrying them.
Small lights bob over {PLACE}, in a line, as if they were going somewhere.

win.say: He follows them to the end and they settle like fireflies in his hair. He feels lucky.

lose.say: The lanterns go out one by one before he catches up.

events.missed: Lanterns floated over {PLACE} last night, and no one lit them.

events.title: A wish comes up the well
text: A voice from {PLACE} asks for someone to make a wish, any wish.
Coins jump out of {PLACE}, one at a time, as if it were giving change.

win.say: He wishes for a good day for the whole street. The water laughs and he finds a coin in his pocket.

lose.say: He wishes for a sandwich. The well sighs and goes quiet.

events.missed: Somebody's wish came true at {PLACE}, they say.

events.title: The statue steps down
text: The statue at {PLACE} has climbed off its stand to stretch its legs.
At {PLACE} the plinth is empty, and heavy stone footsteps head down the street.

win.say: He helps the statue back up before dawn. It nods once and freezes again, a little prouder.

lose.say: By morning the statue is back, facing the wrong way, and the papers blame students.

events.missed: The statue at {PLACE} faces the other way this morning.

events.title: A shadow over the roofs
text: A great winged shadow sweeps over {PLACE}, and the birds go silent.
Above {PLACE} something circles, far bigger than a gull.

win.say: He waves; a single warm scale drifts down into his hands.

lose.say: It's gone behind the clouds before he gets a proper look.

events.missed: Folk at {PLACE} swear they saw a dragon, but nobody has a photo.

events.title: Jackpot fever
text: The jackpot has rolled over five times and the queue at {PLACE} goes round the corner.
A chalkboard outside {PLACE}: JACKPOT TONIGHT, and a queue to match.

win.say: He keeps the queue's spirits up with a song; the kiosk owner slips him a lucky charm.

lose.say: The machine breaks down just as he reaches the front.

events.missed: Everyone in town queued at {PLACE} for the jackpot.

events.title: A cook-off
text: Grills and pots line {PLACE}: a cook-off, and one team is a cook short.
A banner over {PLACE}: the neighbourhood cook-off, all welcome.

win.say: His dish takes second place and the judges ask for seconds.

lose.say: His soup is mostly salt, but he learns from the winners.

events.missed: There was a cook-off at {PLACE}; the smell is still in the air.

events.title: A wall of dreams
text: A chalk wall at {PLACE} reads "Before I die I want to...", with a hundred answers.
Someone has set up a big board at {PLACE}: write one thing on your bucket list.

win.say: He chalks up a dream from his bucket list, and a stranger writes "me too!" under it.

lose.say: The chalk snaps, but he reads every dream on the wall and walks off smiling.

events.missed: There was a wall of dreams at {PLACE}; the rain has washed most of it off.
